groups.summary: The entry points of the heliaPROFILER Python API: one call, one session, and the progress stream they report through.
The run description: what to profile, on what, how, and what to write out. Every field of a YAML config file lands in one of these.
Power capture settings: which instrument measures the rail, how it is wired to the board, and which window of the run is integrated.
The fixed vocabularies a configuration selects from: engines, toolchains, capture transports, memory placements and reset strategies.
What this build of heliaPROFILER is qualified against: the board, engine and toolchain matrix, and the locked dependency revisions a run was produced with.
What a profiling run produces: the run result, its per-layer and PMU detail, and the firmware and run metadata that say how it was measured.
The on-disk index of a run directory: the artifacts it holds, the issues raised against it, and whether its numbers may be used.
What a power capture produces: the measured result, the observations behind it, and the on-device summary the firmware reports.
The provenance of a power number: how it was observed, what the measurement boundary included, and whether the capture holds together.
Comparing two runs and judging one: the comparability rules that decide whether a comparison is meaningful, and the metric policies that turn numbers into a verdict.
The static cost model of a network, read from the model file before anything is built or run.
Collecting a redacted support bundle from a run directory, and reading one back.
The exception hierarchy every heliaPROFILER failure is raised through, rooted at HpxError.
Packaged model and config assets used by the examples, smoke tests and tutorials.
